headline: Madras HC declines to stop DRI action on turbine wheel classification dispute
reference: M/s. Turbo Energy Pvt. Ltd. vs The Chairman, CBIC & Ors., W.P.Nos.39324 and 39329 of 2026, Madras High Court, 19.11.2026 (2026:MHC:4652)
summary_points: Issue: importer sought to restrain DRI from coercive action, seizure and 'voluntary' Section 28(5) payment of about ₹18 crore duty, and sought unedited search video footage.
Dispute: importer classified turbine wheel raw parts under CTI 7508 9090 (nil duty); DRI says CTI 8414 9090 (7.5%) applies as the goods are precision cast.
Held: court declined to interfere, citing DRI's Section 108 powers and the disputed classification; the Section 28(5) prayer was premature and consequential.
Held: video footage request is premature, as granting it mid-investigation would interfere with the probe; both writ petitions dismissed, no costs.
Impact: pending investigation, writ relief against DRI seizure and summons on classification disputes is hard to get; importers should respond on merits before the authorities.
who_is_affected: Importers facing DRI investigation, seizure or Section 28(5) demands over tariff classification, and the advisers handling such cases.
action_required: Review classification records and past assessments, engage with the investigation and adjudication process, and avoid relying on writ petitions to stall DRI inquiries.

Madras High Court: no relief for importer against DRI action in a classification dispute

In M/s. Turbo Energy Pvt. Ltd. vs The Chairman, CBIC (W.P.Nos.39324 and 39329 of 2026, decided 19 November 2026), the petitioner had classified turbine wheel raw parts under CTI 7508 9090 (nil duty). DRI contends they fall under CTI 8414 9090 (7.5%) as precision-cast parts.

The petitioner sought to restrain coercive action, seizure of goods and 'voluntary' payment of about ₹18 crore under Section 28(5) of the Customs Act, and asked for unedited video footage of the search.

The Court declined to interfere. It noted the disputed classification and DRI's powers under Section 108, held the Section 28(5) prayer premature and consequential, and held the footage request premature as it would interfere with the investigation. Both petitions were dismissed with no costs.

Takeaway: while an investigation is on, writ courts are reluctant to step in on classification disputes. Importers should build their merits case for the adjudication stage.

Please verify with the official source before acting.
